source_text: Ὑπόθεσις δὲ αὐτοῖς τῆς ἀποστασίας οἱ ἄνθρωποι γίνονται. Διάγραμμα γὰρ αὐτοῖς ἀστροθεσίας ἀναδείξαντες, ὥσπερ οἱ τοῖς κύβοις παίζοντες, τὴν εἱμαρμένην εἰσηγήσαντο λίαν ἄδικον. Ὅ τε γὰρ κρίνων καὶ ὁ κρινόμενος καθ᾿ εἱμαρμένην εἰσὶ γεγονότες, καὶ οἱ φονεύοντες καὶ οἱ φονευόμενοι, καὶ οἱ πλουτοῦντες καὶ οἱ πενόμενοι, τῆς αὐτῆς εἱμαρμένης ὑπάρχουσιν ἀπογεννήματα· πᾶσα τε γένεσις, ὥσπερ ἐν θεάτρῳ, τερπωλὴν παρέσχε τούτοις, παρ᾿ οἷς, ὥς φησιν Ὅμηρος, Ἄσβεστος δ᾿ ἄρ᾿ ἐνῶρτο γέλως μακάρεσσι θεοῖσιν. Οἱ γὰρ τοὺς μονομαχοῦντας βλέποντες καὶ θάτερος θατέρῳ σπουδάζων, καὶ ὁ γαμῶν καὶ παιδοφθορῶν καὶ μοιχεύων, γελῶν τε καὶ ὀργιζόμενος, φεύγων τε καὶ τιτρωσκόμενος, πῶς οὐχὶ θνητὸς εἶναι νομισθήσεται; Δι᾿ ὧνπερ γὰρ ἑαυτοὺς ὁποῖοί τινες πεφύκασι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις πεφανερώκασι, διὰ τούτων τοὺς ἀκούοντας ἐπὶ τὰ ὅμοια προετρέψαντο. Καὶ μήτι γε οἱ δαίμονες αὐτοὶ μετὰ τοῦ ἡγουμένου αὐτῶν Διὸς ὑπὸ τὴν εἱμαρμένην πεπτώκασι, τοῖς αὐτοῖς πάθεσιν ὥσπερ καὶ οἱ ἄνθρωποι κρατηθέντες; Καὶ ἄλλως δὲ πῶς τιμητέον τούτους παρ᾿ οἷς δογμάτων ἐναντιότης ἐστὶ πολλή; Ῥέαν μὲν γάρ, ἣν οἱ ἀπὸ τῶν Φρυγίων ὁρῶν Κυβέλην φασίν, ἀποτμήσεις αἰδοίων νενομοθετηκέναι διὰ τὸν ἐρώμενον ταύτης Ἄττιν· Ἀφροδίτη δὲ γάμου πλοκαῖς ἥδεται. Μάγος ἐστὶν Ἄρτεμις, θεραπεύει ὁ Ἀπόλλων. Καὶ μετὰ τὴν Γοργοῦς καρατομίαν, τῆς Ποσειδῶνος ἐρωμένης, ἀφ᾿ ἧς Πήγασος ὁ ἵππος καὶ ὁ Χρυσάωρ ἀνέθορε, τὰς σταγόνας τῶν αἱμάτων ἡ Ἀθηνᾶ καὶ Ἀσκληπιὸς διενείμαντο· καὶ ὁ μὲν ἀπ᾿ αὐτῶν ἔσωζεν, ἡ δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν ὁμοίων λύθρων ἀνθρωποκτόνος καὶ πολεμοποιὸς ἐγίνετο.Ταύτην μοι δοκοῦσιν Ἀθηναῖοι μὴ βουληθέντες διαβάλλειν καὶ τὸν ἀπὸ τῆς Ἡφαίστου μίξεως γινόμενον τῇ γῇ προσάπτειν, ἵνα μὴ νομίζηται καθάπερ ἡ Ἀταλάντη διὰ τὸν Μελέαγρον οὕτω καὶ ἡ Ἀθηνᾶ διὰ τὸν Ἥφαιστον τῆς ἀνδρείας ἐστερῆσθαι. Ὁ γὰρ ἀμφιγυήεις, ὡς εἰκός, ὁ πόρπας καὶ γναμπτὰς ἕλικας δημιουργῶν, τοῖς κοροκοσμίοις ἠπάτησε τὴν ἀμήτορα παῖδα καὶ ὀρφανήν. Ποσειδῶν ναυτίλλεται, πολέμοις Ἄρης ἥδεται, κιθαριστής ἐστιν ὁ Ἀπόλλων, Θηβαίοις Διόνυσος τυραννεῖ, Κρόνος τυραννοκτονεῖ. Ζεὺς καὶ θυγατρὶ συγγίνεται, καὶ ἡ θυγάτηρ ἀπ᾿ αὐτοῦ κύει. Μαρτυρήσει μοι νῦν Ἐλευσὶς καὶ δράκων ὁ μυστικὸς καὶ Ὀρφεὺς ὁ Θύρας δ᾿ ἐπίθεσθε βεβήλοις λέγων. Ἀϊδωνεὺς ἁρπάζει τὴν Κόρην, καὶ αἱ πράξεις αὐτοῦ γεγόνασι μυστηρια· κλαίει Δημήτηρ τὴν θυγατέρα, καί τινες ἀπατῶνται διὰ τοὺς Ἀθηναίους. Ἐν τῷ τεμένει τοῦ Λητοΐδου καλεῖταί τις Ὀμφαλός· ὁ δὲ Ὀμφαλὸς τάφος ἐστὶν Διονύσου. Ἐπαινῶ σε νῦν, ὦ Δάφνη· τὴν ἀκρασίαν τοῦ Ἀπόλλωνος νικήσασα ἤλεγξας αὐτοῦ τὴν μαντικήν, ὅτι μὴ προγνοὺς τὰ περὶ σὲ τῆς αὐτοῦ τέχνης οὐκ ὤνατο.Λεγέτω μοι νῦν ὁ ἑκατηβόλος, πῶς Ὑάκινθον διεχρήσατο Ζέφυρος. Ζέφυρος αὐτὸν νενίκηκε· καί, τοῦ τραγῳδοποιοῦ λέγοντος Αὔρα θεῶν ὄχημα τιμιώτατον, ὑπὸ βραχείας αὔρας νικηθεὶς ἀπώλεσε τὸν ἐρώμενον.
pass_a_gloss: The people become a hypothesis of their apostasy to them. For having shown them a diagram of astrothesy, like those playing with dice, they introduced a very unjust fate. For both the one judging and the one being judged have become according to fate, and those killing and those being killed, and those being rich and those being poor, are offspring of the same fate; every birth, like in a theater, provided entertainment to them, to whom, as Homer says, unstoppable laughter arose among the blessed gods. For those watching the ones fighting each other and each one striving against the other, and the one marrying and corrupting children and committing adultery, laughing and getting angry, fleeing and being wounded, how will they not be thought to be mortal? Through which things they have shown themselves to people to be of a certain kind, through these things they have persuaded the listeners to similar things. And will not even the demons themselves, along with their leader Zeus, have fallen under fate, being overcome by the same passions as humans? And otherwise, how are they to be honored by those for whom there is great opposition of doctrines? For example, Rhea, whom the Phrygians call Cybele, has established the cutting off of genitals due to her loved one Attis; Aphrodite delights in the braids of marriage. Artemis is a magician, Apollo provides healing. And after the beheading of Gorgo, the loved one of Poseidon, from which Pegasus the horse and Chrysaor arose, Athena and Asclepius divided the drops of blood; and he saved from them, while she became a murderer of men and a maker of war from similar plunder. It seems to me that the Athenians did not want to slander her and attribute the one born from the union with Hephaestus to the earth, so that Athena would not be thought to have been deprived of courage like Atalanta because of Meleager, and so also because of Hephaestus. For the one who is lame, as is likely, the creator of pots and curved handles, deceived the unloved and orphaned child with his tricks. Poseidon sails, Ares delights in wars, Apollo is a cithara player, Dionysus tyrannizes the Thebans, Cronus kills tyrants. Zeus even unites with his daughter, and the daughter becomes pregnant from him. Eleusis and the mystical dragon and Orpheus of Thrace will now testify to me, saying to the profane. Hades seizes Core, and his actions have become mysteries; Demeter mourns her daughter, and some are deceived through the Athenians. In the temple of Leto's son, someone is called Omphalos; and Omphalos is the tomb of Dionysus. I praise you now, Daphne; having overcome the intemperance of Apollo, you refuted his divination, because not having foreknown the things about you, he was not able to use his skill. Let the Hecate-worshiper tell me now how Zephyr treated Hyacinth. Zephyr defeated him; and, the tragedian saying 'Aura is the most honored vehicle of the gods', having been defeated by a short gust of wind, he lost the one he loved.
pass_b_english: People serve as the hypothesis of their apostasy. Having displayed a diagram of astral arrangement, they introduced a most unjust fate, just like men playing with dice. For both judge and judged exist by fate, as do killers and killed, rich and poor; all are offspring of the same fate. Every birth, as in a theater, gave these beings entertainment. Of them Homer says, 'Unquenchable laughter arose among the blessed gods.' For those who watch men fighting in single combat, each straining against the other, and who watch the man who marries and corrupts children and commits adultery, laughing and raging, fleeing and being wounded — how would they not be thought mortal? Through the very things by which they revealed what sort of beings they are, they persuaded their hearers toward the same things.

Will not even the demons themselves, together with their leader Zeus, have fallen under fate, mastered by the same passions as humans? And in any case, how are these beings to be honored by those among whom there is great opposition of doctrines? Rhea, whom men from Phrygia call Cybele, legislated castration because of her beloved Attis; Aphrodite delights in the braids of marriage. Artemis is a magician, Apollo practices healing. After the beheading of Gorgo, Poseidon's beloved, from whom Pegasus the horse and Chrysaor sprang, Athena and Asclepius divided the drops of blood; from them he saved, while she became a manslayer and war-maker from similar spoils.

It seems to me the Athenians, unwilling to slander her, ascribed the offspring of Hephaestus' union to the earth, lest Athena be thought deprived of courage through Hephaestus just as Atalanta was through Meleager. For the lame god, as is likely, the maker of pots and curved handles, deceived the unloved, orphaned child with his tricks. Poseidon sails, Ares delights in wars, Apollo plays the cithara, Dionysus tyrannizes the Thebans, Cronus kills tyrants. Zeus unites with his own daughter, and the daughter conceives by him. Eleusis and the mystic serpent and Orpheus of Thrace will now testify to me, saying, 'Place the doors, you profane.' Hades seizes Core, and his deeds have become mysteries; Demeter mourns her daughter, and some are deceived through the Athenians. In the precinct of Leto's son a certain place is called Omphalos, and Omphalos is the tomb of Dionysus.

I praise you now, Daphne; overcoming Apollo's intemperance, you refuted his divination, because, not foreknowing the things concerning yourself, he could not avail himself of his own art. Let the far-shooter tell me now how Zephyr treated Hyacinth. Zephyr defeated him; and though the tragedian says, 'Breeze is the most honored vehicle of the gods,' overcome by a brief gust he lost his beloved.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex mythological and philosophical arguments of the Greek text. Pass A preserves the clause structure and nuances (e.g., 'the one judging and the one being judged', 'the one marrying and corrupting children'). Pass B provides a fluent rendering that maintains the meaning of the Greek. All mythological references (Cybele/Rhea, Athena/Hephaestus, etc.) are correctly handled. The translation of 'ἑκατηβόλος' as 'far-shooter' (Pass B) and 'Hecate-worshiper' (Pass A) are both acceptable interpretations of the epithet for Apollo, and the differences do not constitute a failure of fidelity.
